query: Consider the following context: Refractory high-entropy alloys (HEAs) are promising candidates for next-generation nuclear applications, particularly fusion reactors, due to their excellent high-temperature mechanical properties and irradiation resistance. In that context, which material can be used for low-activation structural material for high-temperature plasma-facing components (PFCs) in fusion reactors, and why?

generation.hypothesis: Refractory high-entropy alloys (HEAs) can be used as low-activation structural materials for high-temperature plasma-facing components (PFCs) in fusion reactors.
generation.mechanism: Irradiation resistance and high-temperature mechanical properties
generation.predicted_outcome: HEAs maintain their structural integrity and exhibit low activation under fusion reactor conditions
generation.boundary: Temperature and irradiation limits of HEAs
generation.uncertainty: Lack of specific data on the behavior of HEAs in fusion reactor environments

falsification_experiment.design: Exposure of HEA samples to simulated fusion reactor conditions
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If HEAs exhibit significant degradation or high activation under fusion reactor conditions, the hypothesis is falsified
